newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union leader urges new truckers' talks.
newsitem.headline: French union leader urges new truckers' talks.

text.p: A senior French trade union leader appealed to the government on Thursday to make one more mediation attempt after negotiations between striking truck drivers and employers collapsed during the night over pay.

"Talks must continue," Marc Blondel, head of the Force Ouvriere union told Europe 1 radio. "The big problem is wages." The marathon talks broke down at midnight and the government said mediator Robert Cros' mission was successfully completed.

But truckers kept up barricades for an 11th day on roads around France, strangling the economy. The state traffic information centre said there were 244 barricades on major routes in France early on Thursday.
"I would ask Mr Cros to have another go and I will try to get pressure on the employers," Blondel said. He urged truckers to "stay calm and not reply to provocations" at the roadblocks.

Blondel, whose union is the third largest in France, stopped short of calling for a widening of the dispute to other sectors. He did not rule out the possibility of signing agreements reached on early retirement and working hours during Cros' talks in the absence of an overall deal.

Negotiator Claude Debons of the pro-Socialist CFDT union, France's biggest, told Radio Luxembourg: "In the present situation, especially on the issue of working hours, conditions are not right to lift the barricades."
